notes.deserted_keep_may_be_teleport_only: The Deserted Keep (x3153-3156, z3920-3929) holds `wildoutlever` (1815) at (3153,3923), which teleports to (2562,3311) in Ardougne. Its doorway is real: (3153,3921) and (3154,3921) carry no wall loc. But it has resisted entry from BOTH sides on separate attempts: from the east a character reached (3168,3926) and could not get west; from the west another reached (3141,3921), on the keep's own open row, and could not move 2 tiles east. The blocking ground is unmapped -- the loc data shows only dugupsoil decoration between. WORKING HYPOTHESIS: the keep is teleport-only, and wildoutlever is the EXIT for characters who arrived via the Ardougne lever (1814 at (2561,3311)). If so, the lever is not a way INTO Ardougne for a character who walked to the Wilderness, and Ardougne is reachable only on foot -- which White Wolf Mountain blocks. Worth one more attempt from the north or from inside the walls before treating it as settled. Also noted: floorweb (706) tiles sit inside the keep at (3153,3921),(3152,3923),(3153,3925),(3156,3924) -- untested whether they block or are decoration.
notes.lethal_npc_ids: Dragon ids are NOT contiguous: 53 red, 54 black, 55 blue, 941 GREEN, 50 king, 51 baby, 52 baby blue. Any guard phrased as 'check 53/54/55' misses green entirely -- that is how a character died after the guard was written AND followed. Enumerate by name from npc.pack, or just run mapdata.py band over the corridor you mean to walk.
notes.log_every_hop_even_manual_ones: A raw `clawscape.py act walkTo` bypasses walk.py and therefore records nothing. scout2 crossed the Lumbridge/Varrock boundary with one manual 27-tile hop from (3217,3333) to (3206,3345) and reached Varrock, yet route.py still answered no_known_route because the one hop that mattered was never logged. If you must issue a manual walkTo, record it afterwards with travel.py's record(). Better: use walk.py.
notes.northern_wilderness_needs_short_legs: In the Wilderness band north of z~3850, walkTo legs longer than about 6-8 tiles fail consistently while 6-tile hops go straight through. A route of 13 six-tile steps from (3141,3910) to (3219,3910) landed every leg after every longer-legged attempt over the same ground had reported a stall. Several 'blocked' entries recorded earlier in that region are probably this artefact rather than terrain, so re-test a dead end there with short hops before believing it. This is the same trap as the general rule in mechanics.md, but the threshold is tighter up here than elsewhere.
notes.route_py_cannot_plan_through_crossings: route.py builds its graph only from recorded hops and discards any edge longer than about 9 tiles as a recording artefact -- reasonable, since walkTo caps around 7-8. But the real crossings are legitimate long hops: Lumbridge/Varrock is a single 27-tile walk from (3217,3333) to (3190,3363), and the Al Kharid toll crossing is 6-9 tiles and marked single_hop. So the one edge joining the southern world to Varrock is filtered out, and route.py still answers no_known_route even after a character has walked it and the hop is recorded. CONFIRMED live 2026-09-13: scout2 crossed and reached Varrock; the planner still refuses. The `crossings` list in routes.json holds these, and travel.py consults it, but route.py's graph does not. Fixing that -- letting route.py treat a `crossings` entry as a valid edge regardless of length -- would connect the two halves of the map for every character.
notes.safe_lane_to_the_rogues: A lane threading the above, planned from spawn data rather than walked: hold x3060-3074 through z3805-3825 (west of the green dragons), narrow to x3059-3069 through z3829-3848 (west of the scorpions, east of the black knights), then drift EAST to x3071-3090 before z3871 (east of the spiders, west of the giants and lesser demons), and hold that to the rogues at (3078,3910). UNWALKED -- these spawns wander, so treat it as a hypothesis and carry a full pack. The corridor Claude used, straight up x3078, runs through the dragons.
